matches.found: Tibetan opens 'brgyad pa'i skabs su ni thog mar gnyen po dran 'dzin gyi rtsol ba cung zad bsten na...' — the state is referred to only as 'the eighth', with no name. English opens 'Here is what happens when you reach the eighth state of meditation, called "making the mind single-pointed."'
matches.evidence: The observation is factually correct — rtse gcig tu byed pa, the eighth state's name, does not appear anywhere in C03:210 — but it is the author's consistent practice, not an omission. Every one of the six neighbouring state-by-state segments does the same: C03:206 Tibetan says only 'bzhi pa ni' while the English supplies 'called "placing the mind on the object closely"'; likewise C03:207 ('lnga pa ni' / 'controlling the mind'), C03:208 ('drug pa ni' / 'pacifying the mind'), C03:209 ('bdun pa'i skabs su' / 'pacifying the mind totally') and C03:211 ('dgu pa ni' / 'achieving equilibrium'). The commentary numbers the states; the translator restores the names from the enumeration given earlier at C03:157 and C03:201, where the eighth is 'rtse gcig tu byed pa'. The supplied English name matches that list.
matches.note: Registered as not-an-erratum so the finding is closed rather than left for a future editor to re-derive. The log itself seems to reach the same conclusion — 'Recorded so a reader meets the note rather than the puzzle.' One caveat: the excerpt's first sentence, 'His slip, and it stands', belongs to a preceding item that is not in the excerpt, so I could not identify what slip was meant or confirm that it concerns C03:210. If that sentence names a real defect it is still unregistered, and the source log at line 1242 should be re-read for it.

class_examples.found: THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I GO 'PANG BSGRUB PA
class_examples.expected: THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I GO 'PHANG BSGRUB PA
class_examples.evidence: Confirmed from this segment's own text. ACIP (source of record) reads GO 'PANG; the wylie field carries the same reading, go 'pang, so this is in the source, not the converter. The word is go 'phang (rank, station, state), which is what GMR translates: 'the state of All-Knowing'. Re-derived corpus counts: acip LIKE '%GO ''PANG%' returns exactly one row, C03:445; acip LIKE '%GO ''PHANG%' returns 219; the wylie field splits identically, 1 vs 219. Stronger still, the syllable 'pang occurs NOWHERE else in the corpus wylie: a-chung ('a) prefixes only voiced or aspirated radicals in Tibetan orthography ('g 'j 'd 'b 'dz 'kh 'ch 'th 'ph 'tsh), so 'p- is not a spellable syllable onset and 'pang cannot be a variant. Parallel-witness check: no other segment carries this passage (english LIKE '%habit of hoping for the%', english LIKE '%up to the final end%', wylie LIKE '%tshe ''di snang gi zhen pa%', wylie LIKE '%rang res ngan ''gro%' each return C03:445 alone). The exact collocation mkhyen pa'i go 'p… appears in seven other rows, every one of them 'phang: C01:84, C16:32, TCS02:315, TCS09:37, Sunlight:595, Sunlight:707, SPF:461. The nearest relative for the surrounding idiom, ILL:126 (thog mtha' bar gsum du gal che), shares only that closing idiom and says nothing about go 'phang. Registered classes checked and not applicable: no {SHl} drop, no fused footnote number, no folio marker, no glued heading; the ACIP trailing shad ',' absent from the wylie is the normal strip, and ACIP TSE for wylie tshe is the ACIP convention (TS = tsh), not an error. A dropped aspiration H in one row against 219 correct ones, yielding an impossible syllable, is a keystroke error.
